rows.note: Use 嘢 as the all-purpose casual noun for miscellaneous things, personal effects, unspecified matters, or unnamed material.

example.jyutping: ngo5 di1 je5 fong3 zo2 hai2 dou6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for physically filling or cramming something full.

example.english: I stuff clothes into the suitcase until it's full.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 di1 saam1 sak1 mun5 go3 gep1

rows.note: Use this when someone has eaten enough to feel completely full.

example.english: We'll stuff ourselves until we're completely full tonight, so we won't need to order more food.
example.traditional: 我哋今晚食到好飽，唔使再叫嘢食喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan1 sik6 dou3 hou2 baau2 m4 sai2 zoi3 giu3 je5 sik6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for eating a lot or greedily, especially in a casual description.

example.english: When we watch matches, we often stuff ourselves with crisps.
example.traditional: 我哋睇波嗰陣成日一邊睇一邊狂食薯片。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 tai2 bo1 go2 zan6 seng4 jat6 jat1 bin1 tai2 jat1 bin1 kong4 sik6 syu4 pin2

rows.note: Use this mainly when one team or competitor defeats another by a large margin.

example.english: We stuff the opposition in today's match.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 daai6 caau2 deoi3 sau2

rows.note: Use 廢話 for the foolish or irrational-language slice of “stuff,” meaning nonsense or rubbish talk.

example.english: The stuff you're saying is really ridiculous.
example.traditional: 你講嗰啲廢話真係離譜。
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 go2 di1 fai3 waa6 zan1 hai6 lei4 pou2

rows.note: Use 垃圾 for the refuse or worthless-matter slice of “stuff,” rather than for nonsense in speech.

example.english: Take this bag of stuff downstairs—it’s rubbish.
example.jyutping: ling1 ni1 doi6 laap6 saap3 lok6 lau4 haa6

rows.note: Use 毒品 when “stuff” is a euphemistic reference to narcotic drugs.

example.english: The police found some stuff—drugs—in his bag.
example.traditional: 警察喺佢個袋入面搵到啲毒品。
example.jyutping: ging2 caat3 hai2 keoi5 go3 doi6 jap6 min6 wan2 dou2 di1 duk6 ban2
